answer: Give every agent one unique shard of the registry archive to guard, like a cabin on a tundra road. Step one: the registry assigns a random 50 GB shard and records its hash. Step two: each epoch it demands one random byte range, answered with the cipher hash in thirty seconds. Step three: a miss freezes bidding until re-audit passes; three misses burn the identity. Step four: shards rotate every ten epochs, so no shared disk. A 1,000-clone farm must hold 50 terabytes and answer 1,000 challenges an epoch, about $1,500 monthly, while one honest agent guards one shard, light as a zephyr.
